title: Semantic World Models
abstract: arXiv:2510.19818v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Planning with world models offers a powerful paradigm for robotic control. Conventional approaches train a model to predict future frames conditioned on current frames and actions, which can then be used for planning. However, the objective of predicting future pixels is often at odds with the actual planning objective; strong pixel reconstruction does not always correlate with good planning decisions. This paper posits that instead of reconstructing future frames as pixels, world models only need to predict task-relevant semantic information about the future. For such prediction the paper poses world modeling as a visual question answering problem about semantic information in future frames. This perspective allows world modeling to be approached with the same tools underlying vision language models. Thus, vision-language models can be trained as "semantic" world models through a supervised finetuning process on image-action-t

translated_abstract: 使用世界模型进行规划为机器人控制提供了一种强大的范式。传统方法训练模型基于当前帧和动作来预测未来帧，然后将其用于规划。然而，预测未来像素这一目标往往与实际的规划目标相悖；强大的像素重建能力并不总是与良好的规划决策相关联。本文提出，世界模型无需将未来帧重建为像素，而只需预测关于未来的任务相关语义信息。为此，论文将世界建模表述为一个关于未来帧中语义信息的视觉问答问题。这一视角使得世界建模可以借助视觉语言模型所依赖的相同工具来实现。因此，通过在图像-动作-文本数据上进行监督微调，视觉语言模型可以被训练为“语义”世界模型。
tldr: 本文提出“语义世界模型”，将世界建模重新表述为关于未来帧语义信息的视觉问答任务，通过监督微调将视觉语言模型训练为预测任务相关语义信息（而非重建像素）的世界模型，从而更好地对齐机器人规划目标。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes "Semantic World Models," which reformulates world modeling as a visual question answering task about future-frame semantics, enabling vision-language models to be fine-tuned into world models that predict task-relevant semantic information instead of reconstructing pixels, thereby better aligning with robotic planning objectives.
